note: Cached responses recorded from a local Gemma run, checked by hand. Demo Mode never calls a model.

findings.title: Loop reads one item past the end of the orders array
findings.explanation: The loop condition is i <= orders.length. Array indexes stop at length - 1, so the last pass reads orders[orders.length], which is undefined. orders[i].price then throws a TypeError and the total never comes back.
findings.whyItMatters: This is a classic off-by-one: it works for empty or single-item arrays? No — it fails exactly when the last item is reached, which is every real checkout. Learning to read loop bounds carefully prevents crashes that only appear in production.

findings.title: Recipient names are inserted as HTML (XSS)
findings.explanation: Recipient names are concatenated into an HTML string and assigned with innerHTML. A name like is executed by the browser instead of being displayed as text.
findings.whyItMatters: Cross-site scripting lets an attacker run code in other users’ sessions, steal data and impersonate them. Building DOM nodes with textContent keeps untrusted data as plain text.

findings.title: Malformed JSON crashes the webhook
findings.explanation: JSON.parse(req.body) throws a SyntaxError when the request body is not valid JSON. Nothing catches it, so a single malformed webhook produces an unhandled error instead of a clear 400 response.
findings.whyItMatters: APIs receive bad input all the time. Wrapping external data in try/catch and returning 400 keeps one bad client from breaking the endpoint for everyone.

findings.title: API key committed in source
findings.explanation: MOON_API_KEY is assigned a literal secret value in tracked source code. Everyone with repository access (and every future clone) can read it.
findings.whyItMatters: A committed credential must be treated as leaked: revoke it, rotate it, and load the replacement from an environment variable. Deleting the line alone is not enough because Git history keeps it.
